2734156.name: Ohev Zedek - Chabad
2734156.note: Happenings Magazine (4 Sept 2017, 'Jewish Houses of Worship around Northeast PA'), its entry 'Ohev Zedek, Scranton': 'Although this congregation's synagogue was originally built as a church in 1901, it was sold to the Orthodox congregation two decades later when the area's Jewish population flourished. Today the stately Victorian building welcomes members from the Scranton area. Rabbi Yehuda Itkin has led the synagogue since it became Chabad in 1986.' Ohev Zedek, 1432 Mulberry St, Scranton. The Pennsylvania Department of Corrections (2023) gives Rabbi Yehuda (Leibel) Itkin, Chabad of Scranton's rabbi, as senior rabbi of Ohav Zedek Synagogue in Scranton. Its chabad.org listing went up 2014-10-20. Was 2014 (the listing date, entered as a low fallback until this was found).

117722.name: Chabad of Scranton
117722.note: Happenings Magazine (4 Sept 2017), on its synagogue, Ohev Zedek in Scranton: 'Rabbi Yehuda Itkin has led the synagogue since it became Chabad in 1986.' Rabbi Itkin directs Chabad of Scranton, whose chabad.org listing has Ohev Zedek as its department, and no earlier Chabad of Scranton was found, so it is dated from the synagogue's becoming Chabad. Medium: the year is the synagogue's. CrownHeights.info, 24 June 2008: 'Harav Leibel Itkin a Shliach in Scranton, PA'; COLlive, 10 Dec 2008: a Mumbai memorial in Scranton 'organized by Shliach Laibel Itkin'. So there by 2008; its start not found. Rabbi Yehuda (Leibel) Itkin was also a contract chaplain at SCI Waymart from 1993 (Pennsylvania Dept. of Corrections, 2023) and is senior rabbi of Ohav Zedek in Scranton. Lead: its chabad.org listing (117722) is from the first batch of listings, about 2000-03. Its chabad.org listing went up 2004-07-22, so it existed by 2004 (was 'by 2008').

118628.name: Rohr Chabad Center of Glenview
118628.note: Chicago Tribune (13 Dec 2004, 'Lighting the holiday spirit'; reprinted on chabadillinois.com as 'Religious displays are Glenview's first'): '"We asked the village to help publicize our diversity," said Benjaminson, who moved to Glenview last year as an emissary of the Brooklyn-based Jewish movement responsible for more than 1,000 menorah displays nationwide.' So Rabbi Yishaya Benjaminson came in 2003. Medium: counted back from 'last year'. TribLocal (on CrownHeights.info, 22 Feb 2011): 'Lubavitch Chabad of Glenview, which has operated out of a storefront on Glenview Road for more than five years', moving to the former Glenkirk school building at 701 Harlem Ave. Rabbi Yishaya Benjaminson. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then.

117805.name: Centre Chabad
117805.note: Charidy campaign of 2023 ('Be a candle in Rabbi Chriqui's menorah'): 'For 35 years, Rabbi Chriqui has illuminated our community with the light of Judaism', so Rabbi Shalom Chriqui, its director, has served since about 1988. Low: it counts his service, not the center's start, and the campaign does not name the center. info and lubavitch.com searched by name and director, and a web search). Quebec enterprise register (Registraire des entreprises, open data 'Registre des entreprises', file of Nov 1 2026): 'CENTRE CHABAD' and 'L'ESCALE CHABAD DU NORD' were names of Montreal Chabad's umbrella corporation, 'L'ORGANISATION DE LA JEUNESSE CHABAD LOUBAVITCH' / 'CHABAD LUBAVITCH YOUTH ORGANIZATION' (NEQ 1143241058, a religious corporation constituted May 1 1973, 3429 Peel Street) from the register's start (March 6 1995) until Oct 26 2012; three weeks later, on Nov 16 2012, 'CENTRE CHABAD' (NEQ 1168686542) was constituted at 4691 Van Horne (the listing's address), adding 'Escale Chabad du Nord' in 2016. So the center existed by 1995. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Director: Shalom Chriqui.

117717.name: Chabad of Penn Wynne

earlier.where: Wynnewood: Rabbi Zalman Gerber's house, the Chabad House at Haverford Road and Indian Creek Drive
Wynnewood: a storefront on Manoa Road, across from Congregation Beth Hamedrosh
Wynnewood: Shabbat services in the Family Hall of the Kaiserman JCC

117717.note: Jewish Exponent (12 Aug 2025, 'Chabad of Penn Wynne Continues to Build Up Community'): 'Chabad of Penn Wynne began 20 years ago as tenants of the Kaiserman JCC.' Twenty years before 2025 is 2005, but its chabad.org listing was already up on 2004-07-22 (the first online directory), so the year is put at 2004, the first record, which the round '20 years ago' fits. Low: a round number and a first record, no report of the opening. (The Exponent's 'began as tenants of the JCC' differs from Wikipedia's account, below, that it began in Rabbi Gerber's house.) The Jewish Exponent (CrownHeights.info, 8 Feb 2007): 'A new Torah scroll was completed recently for Chabad of Penn Wynne'; the procession went from the Kaiserman JCC in Wynnewood 'to the ark at the Chabad House on the corner of Haverford Road and Indian Creek Drive' (Rabbi Zalman Gerber). So it existed by early 2007; its start is not stated. Wikipedia (Penn Wynne; no citation): it started in Rabbi Gerber's house, moved to a storefront on Manoa Road soon after Congregation Beth Hamedrosh moved in across the street in 2007, left it when the lease ended in late May 2010, held Shabbat services in the JCC's Family Hall from 5 June 2010, and from Rosh Hashana (Sept) 2020 has been across City Line Avenue in Overbrook Park (now 7571 Haverford Ave). Rabbi Moshe and Devorah Brennan have directed it since 2011 (its About page). Pennsylvania Department of State record (data.pa.gov, 'Registered Businesses in PA Current by County'): 'Chabad of Penn Wynne Inc.' (filing number 0007313983), created June 25 2021. So the filing is after the listing and is not taken as the year. Its chabad.org listing went up 2004-07-22, so it existed by 2004 (was 'by 2007').

117637.name: Chabad Shul of Potomac
117637.note: No founding year found yet (Nov 9: first pass only: CrownHeights.info and lubavitch.com searched by name and director, and a web search for the older centres; not dug into yet). Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Connection Newspapers (Potomac Almanac, 15 June 2004, 'A New Place to Worship'): 'It's been eleven years in the making, but the Chabad Synagogue on Seven Locks Road dedicated its new sanctuary on June 13' (Rabbi Mendel Bluming); the eleven years may count the building project (from about 1993), not the congregation's start, so it is not taken as the year. Director: Mendel Bluming. Washington Jewish Week (on CrownHeights.info, 28 Nov 2012, 'Chabad Father-Son Team Looks Toward Expansion'): in 2000 Rabbi Bentzion and Zlata Geisinsky 'left their work at the Chabad center in Potomac, to found Chabad of Bethesda-Chevy Chase' (established 1999, per listing 118382), so the Potomac center existed by 1999. Rabbi Mendel Bluming has led it 'since 2003' (his own pages); his parents are on its staff. Mendel Bluming's own blog (July 2017): 'Since 2003, Menachem Mendel Bluming has been serving as the rabbi of Chabad Shul of Potomac' (his tenure, not its start).

117810.name: Chabad Chabanel & Maison Belfield
117810.note: No founding report found (Nov 9 first pass: CrownHeights.info and lubavitch.com searched by name and director, and a web search). Quebec enterprise register (Registraire des entreprises, open data 'Registre des entreprises', file of Nov 1 2026): 'CHABAD CHABANEL' is a name of Montreal Chabad's umbrella corporation, 'L'ORGANISATION DE LA JEUNESSE CHABAD LOUBAVITCH' / 'CHABAD LUBAVITCH YOUTH ORGANIZATION' (NEQ 1143241058, a religious corporation constituted May 1 1973, 3429 Peel Street) from the register's start (March 6 1995) until 2013, so the center existed by then; its own corporations 'CENTRE CHABAD CHABANEL' (NEQ 1165365769) and 'MAISON BELFIELD' (NEQ 1165365983) were constituted Aug 22 2008 at 9297 Tolhurst (the listing's address). Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Director: Zushe Silberstein. L'Chaim (issue 1371, 15 May 2015): 'Fifteen years ago, the rabbi founded Maison Belfield as a halfway house for up to six men at a time, offering newly released Jewish inmates shelter, food, clothing, therapy and reintegration assistance' (Rabbi Zushe Silberstein), so Maison Belfield began about 2000; Chabad Chabanel was there by 1995, so 2000 is not the listing's year.

119776.name: Congregation Bais Menachem-Chabad
119776.note: No founding year found yet (Nov 9: first pass only: CrownHeights.info and lubavitch.com searched by name and director; not dug into yet). Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Director: Moshe Wilhelm. Its chabad.org listing (2317 SW Vermont St) is a branch of Chabad Lubavitch of Oregon (listing 118188, 6612 SW Capitol Hwy), which began when Rabbi Moshe Wilhelm arrived in January 1984 (Jewish Federation of Greater Portland, 24 Jan 2020); the congregation's own start is not found, and it is a separate address, so 1984 is not taken as its year.

118888.name: WCRJ Community Center
118888.note: No founding year found yet (Nov 9: first pass only: CrownHeights.info and lubavitch.com searched by name and director; not dug into yet). Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Director: Aharon Sirota. Colorado Secretary of State record (data.colorado.gov, 'Business Entities in Colorado'): 'WCRJ Educational Center' (ID 20231136109, 2023) and 'WCRJ - CENTER FOR JEWISH LIFE' (ID 20251665694, 2025, 295 S Locust St, the listing's address) are later. So the filing is after the listing and is not taken as the year. Intermountain Jewish News (26 Oct 2017, 'VIP: New faces: Rabbi Mendy & Chana Sirota'): WCRJ and Tehilat Hashem are 'the Chabad-affiliated congregation and Russian Jewish community organization founded by the rabbi's father, Rabbi Aharon Sirota' (no year).

118314.name: Chabad of St. Louis Park
118314.note: No founding year found. Dr. Yosef Y. Shagalow's Chabad of St. Louis Park at 2834 Raleigh Avenue in the Dec 2009 lubavitch.com directory (Wayback); today's listing shows no street. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Lead, not checked (Chabadpedia does not open here): a Firecrawl research agent read Chabadpedia's page on Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Shagalow as saying he went out in 5746 (1985-86) as the Rebbe's shliach in Minneapolis and founded a Chabad House there; which center is not stated. Its listing names Rabbi Yehuda Shurpin with Dr. Shagalow.
